subject: Artifact storage capacity & retention tradeoff review — renewal decision
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@registryplus.io>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sales@registryplus.io
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RegistryPlus renewal & capacity options for Redwood

Hi Karthik,

Quick note — your annual plan is up for renewal on 2026-07-15. Given your recent growth in artifact ingress and the new retention requests for compliance-heavy customers, we put together a few options that blend storage tiers, retrieval egress, and a short-term migration credit if you commit to a 12-month reserved tier.

Attached: RegistryPlus_pricing_v3.xlsx (pricing by tier + migration credit)

High-level options:
- Lite: standard S3-backed storage, 90-day retention, no migration credit.
- Standard (recommended): tiered cold storage, 365-day default, 20% discount for annual commit.
- Enterprise+Migration: same as Standard but with a one-time migration credit to cover transfer costs and 2 weeks of parallel runs.

I flagged a few line items you might care about: manifest indexing costs (per-blob), storage class transitions, and cross-region replication. If you want, I can put together an apples-to-apples comparison with Harbor/JFrog/Cloud provider native registry add-ons.

Would you be available for a 30-min sync this week to walk through the tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Sam
Account Exec, RegistryPlus
phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Sam — thanks for the summary and the spreadsheet. Quick context from our side: our retention needs for regulated customers have jumped (some customers need 540d retain), and our CI/CD pipeline artifact churn means cold-object counts are increasing faster than raw GBs. Key asks before any renewal commit:

1) A clear per-blob vs per-GB breakdown (indexing + storage + egress).
2) Practical migration window: how much parallel run-time and what rate limits for bulk pulls?
3) Any constraints for using RegistryPlus with our Buildkite/Cloud-run CI workflows (concurrency/manifest list costs).

Laura and Dev — looping you in for procurement and infra concerns. Can you review the attached pricing and the runbook draft I started in Drive (link below) and flag must-have items?

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-storage-plan

If we can get granular cost buckets, procurement can model a 12-month reserve vs monthly spike strategy. If RegistryPlus can cover migration costs and provide a short trial of the Enterprise tier, that would materially change the recommendation.

Karthik
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi team — following up with the cost breakdown you asked for (highlights below). I’ve included the full workbook for reference.

Summary:
- Indexing (manifest/OCI list): $0.00225 per manifest per month (applies to each repo tag/manifest).
- Storage: Hot $0.03/GB-month, Cool $0.008/GB-month, Cold $0.0015/GB-month.
- Transition: $0.005/GB when moving from hot->cool.
- Egress: $0.09/GB for first 50TB / mo, tiered thereafter.
- Bulk migration: we provide a 2-week migration credit on Enterprise+Migration and up to 5TB of free transfer. Additional transfer billed at $0.02/GB.

Attachment stub: RegistryPlus_pricing_v3.xlsx

We also tested a Buildkite pipeline with our RegistryPlus SDK — concurrency is fine up to 200 parallel pulls; recommended to use manifest batching to reduce indexing calls. We flagged manifest churn as the biggest cost driver.

Happy to set up a demo with our platform engineering specialist if you want to see the manifest/billing telemetry.

Best,
RegistryPlus Sales

Thanks — I pulled the pricing into a quick model (evidence_storage_costs.csv attached) and also sketched a migration runbook (migration_runbook_draft.md). High level takeaways:

- If we move to Standard (365d) and use cold-tier aggressively, 12-month reserved commitment reduces unit cost by ~28% versus monthly.
- Manifest indexing costs could double our bill if we keep current tagging practices. We should require manifest consolidation (fewer tags per deploy) or introduce a lifecycle job to collapse old tags.
- Migration credit (2-week window + 5TB) covers a reasonable initial tranche, but our repo size is 14TB so we'll need staged migration over 6–8 weeks to avoid spikes and CI flakiness.

Action items:
- Dev: validate Buildkite concurrency plan and run a dry-run to measure manifest call rate (INFRA-2345).
- Karthik: push RegistryPlus for an extended migration credit or lower transfer rate for extra TBs.
- Ben: procurement wants to know if we should engage a consultant for the migration. Rough estimate attached.

Attachment stubs: migration_runbook_draft.md, evidence_storage_costs.csv

Laura
Director, Platform Eng
Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-15T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RegistryPlus renewal & capacity options for Redwood

I ran a simulated bubble (Buildkite job) against a subset of our repos last night. Findings:

- Parallel pulls of large layers (100–300MB) cause temporary throttling at ~150 concurrent pulls when combined with CI agents doing image builds.
- Manifest calls per deploy: ~18 average using our current tagging strategy. If we consolidate tags to pruning policy (keep 3 latest), we drop manifest cost by ~60%.
- Dry-run migration throughput: sustained ~400GB/hour using multi-threaded pulls from an on-prem helper; we can parallelize across 12 workers to hit ~4.8TB/day with careful backoff.

Recommendation: accept Enterprise+Migration if RegistryPlus will extend migration credit to 20TB and provide a short-term bump in concurrency limits during cutover. Otherwise we split migration into smaller waves to avoid CI impact.

Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the analysis. Procurement is OK to move forward conditionally: two asks for go/no-go by 2026-06-25:

1) RegistryPlus confirms extended migration credit to 20TB and provides a short-term concurrency bump for cutover.
2) Karthik submits a short one-page approval memo (cost vs. risk tradeoffs + recommended commit length).

If both items are satisfied, procurement will sign a 12-month reserved contract with the Standard tier and Enterprise migration add-on. If not, we will negotiate month-to-month with strict lifecycle policies and schedule a consultant for migration planning.

Ben
